questions: Why do some practical skills seem easier to learn from another person than from written instructions?
What qualities make someone good at teaching a practical skill?
How has technology changed the way people share practical knowledge?
Should schools give practical subjects as much attention as academic subjects?
Which skills do you think people will still need to learn in person in the future?
part2_anchor:
Describe someone who taught you a useful practical skill.

You should say:
- who this person is
- what skill they taught you
- how they helped you learn it
and explain why this skill has been useful to you.

questions: Why do some people find it difficult to get time alone?
Do you think quiet public places are more important in cities than in small towns?
What can make a library or park feel peaceful even when other people are there?
How should shared buildings meet the needs of people who want different levels of noise?
Do you think demand for quiet spaces will change in the future?
part2_anchor:
Describe a quiet place where you like to spend time.

You should say:
- where this place is
- when you usually go there
- what you do there
and explain what makes this a good place for you to be.

questions: Why do ordinary objects sometimes become important to people?
Do younger and older people tend to value the same kinds of possessions?
How can moving home affect what people choose to keep?
What difficulties arise when museums decide which everyday objects to collect?
Do you think digital records can replace physical objects as reminders of the past?
part2_anchor:
Describe something you have kept for a long time.

You should say:
- what the item is
- how you first got it
- where you keep it
and explain why you have decided to keep it.

questions: What makes a local event attractive to people of different ages?
Why do some residents rarely take part in events in their neighbourhood?
How important are volunteers to the success of community events?
Should local events mainly serve residents or also try to attract visitors?
How might the way communities organise events change in the future?
part2_anchor:
Describe an event in your local area that you enjoyed attending.

You should say:
- what the event was
- who you went with
- what happened at the event
and explain why you enjoyed it.

questions: Why do some people enjoy solving practical problems?
When is it better to ask for help than to solve a problem alone?
How can schools encourage children to try different solutions?
Does easy access to online advice make people more independent?
How should workplaces treat mistakes made while someone is trying a new solution?
part2_anchor:
Describe a time when you solved a practical problem.

You should say:
- what the problem was
- what you did to solve it
- whether anyone helped you
and explain how you felt after dealing with the problem.

questions: What motivates adults to begin learning something unfamiliar?
What can prevent people from taking up a new activity?
How is learning for enjoyment different from learning for work?
Should employers support employees who study subjects unrelated to their jobs?
Do you think people will spend more of their lives learning in the future?
part2_anchor:
Describe an activity you would like to learn to do.

You should say:
- what the activity is
- how you became interested in it
- how you would begin learning it
and explain why you would like to learn this activity.

questions: Why do people take photographs of ordinary daily activities?
How has the ease of taking photographs changed which moments people record?
What can a photograph tell us about the past that written records cannot?
What problems can arise when people share photographs of others online?
Do you think printed photographs will remain popular?
part2_anchor:
Describe a photograph that is important to you.

You should say:
- what the photograph shows
- when it was taken
- how you keep or display it
and explain why it is important to you.

questions: What makes a conversation enjoyable for the people taking part?
Why might people find it easier to talk to strangers in some situations than in others?
How do conversations between different generations benefit people?
Has messaging changed the way people handle disagreements?
Should good listening be taught explicitly at school?
part2_anchor:
Describe a person you enjoy having conversations with.

You should say:
- who this person is
- how you know them
- what you usually talk about
and explain why you enjoy talking to this person.

questions: What should be the main priorities when designing a public building?
Why do some public buildings become important symbols of a place?
How can older buildings be made easier for everyone to use?
When is it better to replace a public building than to renovate it?
Should local people have a say in how public buildings are designed?
part2_anchor:
Describe a public building you have visited.

You should say:
- what the building is used for
- when you went there
- what you noticed about it
and explain what you liked or disliked about this building.

questions: Why is choosing a gift easy for some people and difficult for others?
How important is the amount of money spent on a gift?
Have expectations about gift-giving changed between generations?
What are the advantages of giving experiences rather than objects?
Should people tell others exactly what they would like to receive?
part2_anchor:
Describe a gift you received that you found useful.

You should say:
- what the gift was
- who gave it to you
- how you used it
and explain why this gift was useful to you.

questions: What kinds of tasks are usually done better by a group than by one person?
Why can it be difficult to divide work fairly within a group?
What should a group leader do when members disagree?
Has working online made cooperation easier or more difficult?
How can schools assess individual effort in group projects?
part2_anchor:
Describe an occasion when you worked with other people to achieve something.

You should say:
- what you were trying to achieve
- who you worked with
- what your own contribution was
and explain what you learned from working with these people.

questions: Why do people sometimes ask for advice but then ignore it?
What makes a person seem trustworthy as a source of advice?
When is professional advice more useful than advice from friends or family?
How can people judge the quality of advice they find online?
Should parents let children make decisions that they believe are unwise?
part2_anchor:
Describe a time when someone gave you helpful advice.

You should say:
- what you needed advice about
- who gave you the advice
- what you did after hearing it
and explain why the advice was helpful.

questions: What encourages people to spend more time outdoors?
Do children today have the same opportunities for outdoor play as children in the past?
How should parks accommodate people who want to do different activities?
What problems can arise when a natural area becomes a popular place for recreation?
Who should pay for maintaining public outdoor facilities?
part2_anchor:
Describe an outdoor activity you enjoy doing.

You should say:
- what the activity is
- where you usually do it
- who you usually do it with
and explain why you enjoy this activity.

questions: What makes an educational programme engaging?
How can viewers tell whether a programme presents reliable information?
Is there a risk that entertainment can distract from the educational purpose of a programme?
How has the availability of short videos changed the way people learn?
Should public broadcasters give more time to educational programmes?
part2_anchor:
Describe a programme or video that taught you something interesting.

You should say:
- what it was about
- when you watched it
- what you learned from it
and explain why you found it interesting.

questions: What motivates people to help someone they do not know?
Why do some kinds of voluntary work receive more attention than others?
How can organisations make it easier for people to volunteer?
Should volunteering be a required part of school education?
What support do regular volunteers need so they can continue their work?
part2_anchor:
Describe a person you know who often helps other people.

You should say:
- who this person is
- what kind of help they provide
- how you became aware of what they do
and explain what you admire about this person.

questions: How do visitors decide which places are worth seeing?
Why do residents and tourists sometimes have different opinions about the same place?
What effects can online recommendations have on a small local business?
How can an area welcome visitors without making everyday life difficult for residents?
Is it better for a place to attract many short visits or fewer longer stays?
part2_anchor:
Describe a place in your area that you would recommend to a visitor.

You should say:
- where the place is
- what a visitor can do there
- when it is best to visit
and explain why you would recommend this place.

questions: What makes a household object easy to use?
Why do people sometimes buy products with features they rarely need?
How important is it for everyday products to be easy to repair?
Should manufacturers provide the same design for everyone or different designs for different users?
Do you think people are becoming too dependent on convenient devices?
part2_anchor:
Describe an object that makes your daily life easier.

You should say:
- what the object is
- how you obtained it
- how you use it
and explain how it makes your daily life easier.

questions: Why do people mark important events with celebrations?
How have family celebrations changed in recent years?
What can make a celebration enjoyable without spending much money?
Should communities preserve traditions that few young people take part in?
How might living far from family affect the way people celebrate?
part2_anchor:
Describe a celebration you enjoyed.

You should say:
- what was being celebrated
- where the celebration took place
- what you did during the celebration
and explain what made it enjoyable for you.

questions: What do people learn in everyday life that is difficult to teach in a classroom?
How can employers recognise skills gained through informal experience?
Why might someone prefer learning independently to attending a course?
What role can libraries and community centres play in adult education?
Will formal qualifications become more or less important in the future?
part2_anchor:
Describe something useful you learned outside school or college.

You should say:
- what you learned
- where you learned it
- how you learned it
and explain how it has helped you.

questions: Why do people enjoy listening to stories?
What can fictional stories help people understand about real life?
How does hearing a story differ from reading it?
Why do some stories remain popular for many generations?
Should historical stories be changed to appeal to modern audiences?
part2_anchor:
Describe a story that you found interesting.

You should say:
- what the story was about
- where you read or heard it
- what you remember most clearly
and explain why it interested you.
